title: 1971 AHSME Problem 31
statement: Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is inscribed in a circle with side \(AD,\) a diameter of length \(4.\) If sides \(AB\) and \(BC\) each have length \(1,\) then side \(CD\) has length:

solutions.text:
The circle has radius \(2.\) Let the central angles subtending the equal chords \(AB\) and \(BC\) each be \(2t.\) Then \[ 1=4\sin t, \] so \(\sin t=\frac{1}{4}.\) The remaining central angle from \(C\) to \(D\) along the semicircle is \(\pi-4t,\) hence \[ \begin{aligned} CD&=4\sin\left(\frac{\pi-4t}{2}\right)\\ &=4\cos(2t)\\ &=4\left(1-2\cdot\frac1{16}\right)\\ &=\frac72. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Equal chords \(AB\) and \(BC\) subtend equal central angles
If half of either central angle is \(t\), then \(4\sin t=1\) and \(CD=4\cos(2t)\)
